newsitem.title: FRANCE: Spanish daily fined for libelling French police.
newsitem.headline: Spanish daily fined for libelling French police.

text.p: A Paris court fined the publisher and three reporters of the Spanish daily El Mundo on Friday for reporting allegations that a French police chief helped Spanish death squads wage war on Basque refugees.
The court fined them 40,000 francs ($8,000) each for libel.

It ordered publisher Alfonso de Salas Castellano and the reporters to pay a total 160,000 francs ($32,000) in damages to policeman Joel Cathala, former head of border police in the French Basque region.

Cathala sued El Mundo for publishing allegations by former Spanish Basque official Angel Lopez Carrillo who said he paid Cathala 1.5 million francs ($300,000) for intelligence on Basque separatist exiles, the court was told.
The court said the newspaper and the journalists "failed in their duty of objectivity" by reporting the allegations without double-checking with other sources including Cathala.
It said risks of political manipulation had been high as the report was published in an election year.

Lopez Carrillo had said French documents were used by the Anti-terrorist Liberation Groups (GAL) death squads in 1983-87 to attack suspected ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) separatist guerrillas sheltering in France, the court heard.
He was unable at last month's court hearing to describe precisely Cathala's office where he was alleged to have handed him cash five times between 1984 and 1987.

Cathala has denied the allegations and recalled that his forces had detained several ETA leaders in the period when GAL was active. Policemen supported him in court, saying French police had no reason to help death squads who meant trouble for French police by causing unrest in the Basque region.

The shadowy GAL killed 27 people in France in the 1980s. Among the dead were several French nationals mistaken for members of ETA which has killed hundreds of people in Spain in a campaign for a separate Basque state.

The GAL's "dirty war" has turned into a major scandal in Spain where a former interior minister and other top Socialists were charged with funding the death squads. The Spanish supreme court decided this week in a split ruling against questioning former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez about the scandal.
